method: Native Selenium key actions in actual Chrome/Edge; read-only DOM focus observations and visual inspection of original screenshots. No injected focus, CSS changes or image editing.
findings: General: number -> reason -> Save by Tab; Shift-Tab reverses this order. Required-reason validation leaves focus on Save and retains the draft without a request. Successful save leaves document body focused.
Category arrows/Enter select the focused tab; screenshots show the existing grey focus background and underline.

Email: recipient -> Close -> Send. At the boundary, English Chrome/Edge and Arabic Edge reported BODY before returning to recipient; Arabic Chrome returned directly to recipient. This observation is not a new universal focus-trap requirement.
Repeated Shift-Tab at the recipient boundary kept focus on recipient in the recorded journeys. Invalid-recipient feedback leaves focus on Send. Escape restores Test Send; the next Tab reaches Save.
Browse: dialog container on open, then Close and first scheme; Shift-Tab returns to Close. Escape restores Browse.

Drawer entry leaves the drawer container focused; breadcrumb, custody and audit navigation leave BODY focused. The next Tab after breadcrumb reaches Dashboard; after audit it reaches Refresh. The audit setting chooses its category, not automatic field focus.
Visible field borders and button/tab highlights were reviewed in English and Arabic. Page-level focus has no control highlight. Preserve these existing behaviors; no focus redesign is included.
limits: This completes the scoped pilot baseline, not a whole-application accessibility certification.
Firefox, Safari and CI remain deferred by user instruction.
initial_attempt: An added test assumed dialog Tab wrapping; it failed on existing behavior. The unsupported expectation was removed and the observed boundary explicitly recorded. Initial failures are retained.
